transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-20
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Ava (QuantifyCo PM), Liam (QuantifyCo Head of Cloud Partnerships), Sofia (QuantifyCo Sales)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'll kick off — quick agenda, pipeline review, technical fit on the top deals, security asks, and then next steps. Sound good?
[00:08] Ava: Yep sounds good. Thanks Jordan.
[00:11] Liam: Yeah thanks, appreciate it.
[00:15] Jordan: Cool. First up, top five joint opportunities — I'm going to run through stage and our recommended co-sell motion. Deal one is Enterprise Corp, big SLED, currently in evaluation stage. QuantifyCo has introduced us, looking at a private deployment because of data residency, right?
[00:32] Ava: Correct, they are strict on residency and say they need on-prem or VPC. probable VPC.
[00:37] Maya: From a technical perspective for Enterprise Corp, Private (VPC) is feasible. We'll want to confirm network egress and KMS integration. Also we should look at Dedicated as a mid option if they accept regional hosting. There's some nuance w/ their latency SLOs.
[00:52] Sofia: Question — how different is Dedicated vs Private for procurement? Their procurement team usually avoids on-prem.
[00:58] Jordan: Good question. Dedicated is usually simpler since it's Redwood-managed infra but reserved capacity; Private means we give more control to the customer — more procurement hoops. We'll spell that out in the co-sell deck.
[01:09] Ava: For timing, Enterprise Corp wants pilot in Q3, procurement timeline mid-June.
[01:15] Jordan: Noted. Second deal, FinSight — proof of concept scoped, QuantifyCo is close on their own CRM contact, looks like Hosted API could be fine. Stage is proposal.
[01:27] Liam: FinSight is price sensitive; they've mentioned cost per token is a big blocker.
[01:32] Maya: For cost-sensitive workloads, we can propose quantized models and batching config. Redwood Optimize suggestions usually move the unit cost down 20-40% depending on patterns. We'll prepare a cost model.
[01:44] Jordan: Great. Third is RetailX, mid-market. They're more interested in embedding search — embeddings call. Stage is discovery.
[01:52] Ava: RetailX asked about MRR pricing and whether we support hybrid setups.
[01:56] Maya: Hybrid is possible, yes — you can pin model versions in Private while using Hosted for overflow. That matches our smart routing feature.
[02:06] Jordan: Okay, those are the high level. Now the security asks — Enterprise Corp had an RFP with SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs, and data residency. Ava, can you confirm which of those they flagged as blockers?
[02:20] Ava: SOC2 is must, SSO is required, KMS they want BYOK probably, and audit logs for admin. They also asked about export controls.
[02:30] Maya: We have SOC 2 and can support SSO/SAML and KMS integrations; BYOK is supported for Private or on-prem. For Hosted we can integrate customer KMS with some limitations — need to check the key rotation policy.
[02:44] Jordan: I'll include the security matrix in the deck. Might be good to put an explicit row for BYOK and where it's supported — Hosted, Dedicated, Private.
[02:52] Ava: Yes please. That will speed procurement.
[02:55] Jordan: Quick aside — Enterprise Corp also asked about performance benchmarks, they want 100 qps at 200ms p95 for shorter prompts. Maya, do we think that's realistic on Dedicated?
[03:06] Maya: 200ms p95 at 100 qps is aggressive but approachable with Dedicated with optimized kernels and KV cache if most requests have prefix reuse. For Private, depends on customer hardware. We'll need to run a benchmark.
[03:19] Liam: They can't accept more than 300ms p95 at launch.
[03:22] Maya: Okay, that gives us some headroom. We'll propose a benchmark plan to validate.
[03:27] Jordan: Action: Maya to draft benchmark plan, include perf matrix, sample prompts, token lengths.
[03:33] Ava: Sounds good. For the demo materials, QuantifyCo's AEs want a co-branded deck. Do you have a template?
[03:40] Jordan: Yes, I'll share a co-sell deck and one-pager. Link: https://redwood.internal/sales/cosell-deck (note: placeholder). We'll customize with Dedicated vs Private callouts per deal.
[03:50] Sofia: Also can we include pricing bands? We need ballpark numbers for Enterprise Corp to take to procurement.
[03:55] Jordan: We'll give ranges and called-out assumptions: token volumes, retention, model choice. For the big one we'll suggest a reserved capacity proposal (Dedicated) with an optional Private uplift.
[04:06] Ava: On the procurement front, Enterprise Corp requires a data processing addendum and certain SLA clauses. Do you have a standard DPA?
[04:14] Jordan: We do. I'll attach the DPA and the SOC 2 report.
[04:17] Maya: FYI, if they need audit logs retention for 7 years that becomes a storage cost line item; flag that in the pricing.
[04:26] Liam: Good point, they mentioned longer retention.
[04:28] Jordan: Let's move to deal-specific asks. For Enterprise Corp, QuantifyCo will coordinate an intro to their SLED champion — action for Ava to share contact. For FinSight Jordan will send pricing bands and Optimization suggestions.
[04:42] Ava: I'll share the SLED contact by Friday.
[04:44] Jordan: Great — for RetailX, we should get an initial eval dataset so we can calculate embedding costs.
[04:51] Sofia: I'll ask RetailX for a sample set.
[04:54] Jordan: Ok next — enablement and success plan. QuantifyCo mentioned they want a joint webinar for pipeline enablement in June. Would you like Redwood to co-run?
[05:02] Ava: Yes, that would help. We want a 45-minute session showing joint value props and a short live demo.
[05:08] Maya: We can do a lightweight demo using Hosted for live portion and show Dedicated slides for enterprise architecture.
[05:14] Jordan: I'll propose June 12th for the webinar.
[05:18] Liam: Works for our enablement calendar.
[05:20] Jordan: Anything else on risk or blockers from your side?
[05:23] Ava: One thing — Enterprise Corp legal asked about subprocessor list and onboarding times; they want an SLA on incident response.
[05:30] Jordan: We'll provide subprocessors list and incident response SLAs. For legal timelines, we typically see 3-6 weeks for enterprise contracts but can accelerate with exec sponsor.
[05:40] Sofia: Do you have a standard exec intro template? We want a one pager for exec alignment.
[05:44] Jordan: Yep, one-pager with the proposed commercial terms and risk callouts. I'll send that with the deck.
[05:50] Maya: Quick technical note — if Enterprise Corp uses hardware HSM for KMS, we need to confirm compatibility with our KMS integrations; that sometimes causes delays.
[05:58] Ava: I'll surface that to their infra team.
[06:00] Jordan: Final run — recap of next steps: Jordan send deck + DPA + SOC2 by 5/22, Maya draft benchmark plan by 5/23, Ava share SLED contact by 5/23, schedule benchmark week of 5/26, joint AE call 5/28. Any objections?
[06:16] Liam: No objections.
[06:17] Sofia: All good.
[06:19] Jordan: Awesome. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the repo link for docs. Thanks everyone.
[06:25] Ava: Thanks.
[06:27] Jordan: Bye.

Notes about transcript: occasional mis-heard words, e.g., "SLED" sometimes transcribed as "sled" or "slid", "BYOK" sometimes "BY OK"; speaker labels may shift in auto-transcript. References to redwood internal links are placeholders for shared artifacts.
